description.value: Bao Bei is a well-established modern Chinese restaurant in Vancouver's Chinatown, serving small plates inspired by Taiwanese and Chinese flavours with global influences. The intimate space includes a dining room, high-tops, and a full bar, with both reservations and walk-in seating available. Vegetarian and vegan adaptations are readily offered, making it a welcoming stop for cyclists with varied dietary needs.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: Website content is available and confirms OSM address (163 Keefer Street, Vancouver BC, V6A 1X3) and phone (604 688 0876). The About+FAQ page explicitly addresses vegetarian/vegan and gluten-free friendliness. No mention of bike parking, bike racks, water refill, takeout, or Wi-Fi anywhere on the site, so those remain null per evidence rules. The website retains visible Squarespace template placeholder text in its contact-form boilerplate, though actual contact details are correct.
concerns: Website retains visible Squarespace template placeholder text in the contact-form boilerplate ('123 Street Avenue, City Town, 99999', 'email@address.com', '(123) 555-6789') — actual contact details elsewhere on the site are correct, but suggests the site is only partially maintained.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Bao Bei is a legitimate, operating restaurant with veg/vegan options that cyclists would value, but no cycling-specific amenities (bike parking, water refill, washroom confirmation) are evidenced on the website. A human reviewer should check for nearby bike parking before including.

Vegetarian / vegan / GF.detail: Website FAQ states: 'Are you vegetarian/vegan friendly? Yes, our menu items can easily be adjusted to be meat free.' Gluten-free is flagged as difficult: 'soy sauce is fermented with wheat and it is a primary ingredient in most of the menu.'

wow_evidence: well-established modern Chinese restaurant in Vancouver's Chinatown, serving small plates inspired by Taiwanese and Chinese flavours
